Quick update from infra after a short triage of the 06/07 08:08–08:12 UTC window: we observed an internal load balancer time spike (latency ~700–1200ms) that coincided with increased 502/504 errors returned to the client pool. Several client SDKs in the sample appear to implement conservative retry logic that replayed requests without idempotency tokens, resulting in repeated generation calls that were priced as separate tokens.

What we found:
- Retry bursts aligned to the LB latency spike at 08:09:42 UTC (server traces attached: retry-trace-logs-20260607.log).
- In a subset of calls the client sent identical payloads that produced identical outputs; however, because there was no idempotency header set, each replay was counted as a new request.
- Token accounting at the gateway is per-request; we have no automated dedupe without idempotency headers or KV caching for those specific endpoints.

Proposed remediation:
1) Immediate: we can propose a one-time credit for the duplicated calls in the window. I attached a CSV with sampled requests and token counts; preliminary over-count estimate is ~2.8x for the affected user sessions.
2) Short-term engineering: enable optional request-level idempotency enforcement for generation endpoints for Enterprise accounts (config flag) to prevent double-billing on retries. This requires a minor gateway change and rollout (2–3 weeks).
3) Billing ops: coordinate a proportional credit and a goodwill carry-forward (suggested: 60% automatic credit of the delta + 40% case-by-case review).

I'll attach the traces and a sampled token export to help quantify.

-David
David Kim
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Aline — thanks for your patience and for sharing the sample. Summary and proposed next steps below.

Summary:
- Root cause: transient LB latency spike triggered client retries; client SDKs replayed requests without idempotency, which our gateway counted as separate requests. Engineering estimate: ~2.8x duplication for affected sessions during the 08:08–08:12 UTC window.

Proposed remediation (agreement request):
- Redwood will issue a provisional credit equal to 70% of the measured overage for the identified window while we finalize a full audit (expected in 5 business days).
- We'll implement an optional idempotency-enforcement flag for Enterprise customers; timeline: feature rollout in ~2–3 weeks.
- Finance: Redwood will apply the provisional credit to your next invoice; if final audit reduces the credit, we'll reconcile.

Marissa — can you prepare the provisional credit memo and the credit note PDF for StreamLabs (proposed-credit-summary-StreamLabs.pdf)? Please include the calculation and the recovery/reconciliation plan.

Aline — let us know if this approach works and if you need SPA/procurement paperwork for the invoice hold.

Best regards,
